---
title: Mesh
---

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import mikeio
```

## Read mesh file

A mesh file holds the mesh topology — a set of Nodes and Elements — with no dynamic data. Load it with `mikeio.Mesh`:

```{python}
msh = mikeio.Mesh("../data/odense_rough.mesh")
msh
```

## Plot mesh

Visualize the mesh structure and boundary nodes:

```{python}
msh.plot()
```

```{python}
msh.plot.boundary_nodes(boundary_names=['Land','Open boundary']);
```

## Convert mesh to shapely

Convert the mesh to a [shapely](https://shapely.readthedocs.io/en/latest/manual.html) `MultiPolygon` (requires `shapely`):

```{python}
mp = msh.to_shapely()
mp
```

Now a lot of methods are available, e.g. computing the area and extents:

```{python}
mp.area
```

```{python}
mp.bounds
```

Create a buffered copy of the domain, and extract the coastal zone (the ring within 500 m of the boundary):

```{python}
domain = mp.buffer(0)
domain
```

```{python}
open_water = domain.buffer(-500)

coastalzone = domain - open_water
coastalzone
```

## Check if points are inside the domain

Test individual points against the shapely polygon:

```{python}
from shapely.geometry import Point

p1 = Point(216000, 6162000)
p2 = Point(220000, 6156000)
print(mp.contains(p1))
print(mp.contains(p2))
```

The same check is available directly on the mesh geometry:

```{python}
p1p2 = [[216000, 6162000], [220000, 6156000]]
msh.geometry.contains(p1p2)
```

```{python}
ax = msh.plot()
ax.scatter(p1.x, p1.y, marker="*", s=200, c="red", label="inside")
ax.scatter(p2.x, p2.y, marker="+", s=200, c="green", label="outside")
ax.legend();
```


## Spatial queries

### Find element containing a point

Use `find_index()` to find the element that contains a given point:

```{python}
g = msh.geometry
idx = g.find_index(coords=[216000, 6162000])
idx
```

### Find nearest elements

Use `find_nearest_elements()` to find the closest element centers:

```{python}
g.find_nearest_elements([216000, 6162000], return_distances=True)
```

```{python}
g.find_nearest_elements([216000, 6162000], n_nearest=3)
```

### Boundary polygons

Extract the mesh boundary as polygons, e.g. to inspect the exterior ring:

```{python}
bnd = g.boundary_polygons
exterior = bnd.exteriors[0]
exterior.xy.shape
```


## Change z values and boundary code

The mesh nodes carry z coordinates that can be edited in place. Here we enforce a minimum depth of 2 meters: 

```{python}
g = msh.geometry
print(f'max z before: {g.node_coordinates[:,2].max()}')
zc = g.node_coordinates[:,2]
zc[zc>-2] = -2
g.node_coordinates[:,2] = zc
print(f'max z after: {g.node_coordinates[:,2].max()}')
```

Also change the open boundary (code 2) to a land boundary (code 1):

```{python}
c = g.codes
c[c==2] = 1
g.codes = c
```

## Save the modified geometry to a new mesh file

Write the edited geometry to a new file with `to_mesh()`:

```{python}
g.to_mesh("new_mesh.mesh")
```
